name: SIM identifiers (ICCID, IMSI)
plain: Blocked for normal apps on Android since 10 and never available on iOS.
meaning: SIM IDs identify the subscriber. Only carrier-privileged apps can read them.

limits.headline: Can't see SIM identifiers like ICCID or IMSI as a normal app
limits.user_action: Nothing. Only carrier approved apps get these
can: Use them if it holds carrier privileges (Android)
Get them in a carrier app with an Apple entitlement (iPhone)
cannot: See them on Android 10 and later as a normal app
See them on iPhone as a normal app
Unlock them with a permission prompt
limits.differs: Android allows it for carrier privileged apps; iPhone allows it for carrier apps with an entitlement.

story.what_it_is: Blocked: normal apps cannot read the SIM card's identifying numbers.
story.for_you: You never notice. Apps cannot read the numbers that identify your SIM card or subscriber. Only the carrier's own apps can, so your mobile line stays private.
story.for_makers: A SIM ID is a strong key for a person. It was used for tracking and fraud tricks, so platforms blocked normal apps. Carrier and security teams can still use it through special rights.

use_cases.example: A fraud team wanted to know if a SIM was swapped and now uses carrier checks.
An ad network wanted a SIM ID to follow a person across phones and cannot.
A mobile money app wanted the SIM to confirm the owner and uses a text code.
A carrier app reads the SIM to show the plan.
A travel eSIM app wanted to check the SIM and uses its own flow.
A game wanted to block a banned player by SIM and cannot.
A usage SDK wanted a lifetime SIM count and uses install IDs.

story.android_note: Since Android 10 only apps with carrier privileges can read SIM IDs, and others get an error.
story.ios_note: iPhone has never exposed them to normal apps. Carrier apps need a special entitlement.
